method: static-only: javap -c on the named 26.1 server-game jar (Mojang-mapped; client jar for render/client-only classes), Rust source comparison 26.2 -> 26.1 (read-only), prepared 26.1 data (items.json, registries.json, block-behaviours.json, tags, trade sets, loot tables), jar-data scans. No driver was run, no code executed, no fixes, no edits under versions/26.1/, no commits. Oracle statuses are Batch 0's MEASURED table (docs/sweep/26.1/batch-0-oracles.json); every failing oracle's first error was additionally javap-verified against the 26.1 jar. Programmatic comparisons: FuelValues.vanillaBurnTimes vs the Rust fuel table (64 entries exact), PotionBrewing.addVanillaMixes vs brewing mixes (63 potion + 2 container, exact set and order), trade-set numbers vs int_provider (68/68 sets float amount).
name: Block entities + containers
out_of_scope_failures: drivers in other batches' scope (bonus_chest, decorated_region, storage_alias, food_storage, server_player_sculk, shulker_bullet, held_item_stack, finalize_spawn, natural_spawn, screen_layout, text_display_render); unmeasured drivers with no oracle (test_disconnect_crafting, test_hive_default_patch); Batch 10 items not double-counted (VanillaTextDisplayRenderOracle, VanillaLoomScreenOracle, ParityFont); Batch 2 item not double-counted (VanillaBlockUpdateOracle, 32 errors); Batch 7 overlap noted on B4-G26 (shared loot engine)
systemic_note: The 1.21.7 systemic cause (26.x component/tag logic carried into a version that lacks those lookups) is present again for 26.1, in the opposite direction from 26.2: the 26.1 port was written largely against 26.3's forms, and 26.1's vanilla differs from 26.3 in more places than 26.2's does. Thirteen of the 22 behaviour defects are 26.3-form leaks (furnace >=/remainder, cartography tag gate, smoker/blast halving, mud tag spelling, setEntityData merge, merchant mayPickup, exploration exclusion, hero f32, immediate level-up, merchant float numbers, loot key forms, furnace/sign save formats, pot-sherds compound form, crafter trigger key). Two of the three 1.21.7 majors are fixed (furnaces light, brewing brews); the third (cartography) reproduces and a new major was found (merchant float numbers: zero offers from every trade set). Oracle breakage is heavier than 26.2's: 18 of 34 in-scope oracles pass; the 16 failures are dominated by 26.3-only APIs (EntityTypes, Prediction, EntitySpawnRequest, UvMapping, renderpearl, 26.3 ContextMap, datapackWorldRegistries) plus the fuelValues() abstract-method gap and three cascades on the broken BlockUpdateOracle.
